Brand Concept

Forge the Future

AURIX exists at the point where a raw idea becomes a working machine. The mark already says this: brushed steel for engineering discipline, a live circuit line for intelligence, a cyan glow for the spark that starts it all. Every touchpoint of the event — poster, badge, backdrop, screen — should read as an extension of that same object: precise, metallic, quietly powerful.

Keep the tone technical rather than playful. Think machine shop and mission control, not cartoon robots. Language, layout and color should feel assembled, not decorated — every line earns its place the way a wire earns its trace on a circuit board.

The tagline already gives the event its structure. Use it as the narrative spine for the whole two days — on the poster, on stage, in the opening video — rather than inventing a separate theme line.

Color System

Palette

A dark, metallic base carries the brand everywhere — screens, banners and the stage backdrop. Cyan is the voice of the brand and should always feel earned, not decorative; orange is used sparingly, only where real energy or urgency is needed (countdowns, CTAs, the finals). Tap any swatch to copy its hex code.

Void 52% Gunmetal 23% Cyan 17% Orange 8%
Backgrounds dominate Cyan for the brand voice Orange only for action / energy

On-screen / digital

Void base + Chrome type

Print / brochures

Paper #F7F9FB + Ink #0B1420

Typography

Two Typefaces, Clear Jobs

Orbitron carries the brand's geometry — it's for moments that should feel engineered, not typed. Titillium Web does the actual communicating: subheads, body copy, buttons, captions. Never swap their jobs.

Orbitron — DisplayWeights used: 700 / 800 / 900 · Event name, hero headlines, big stats only

Logo & Usage

Handle It Like Hardware

Clear space: keep an empty margin at least the height of the small circuit node on the mark free of text or other graphics, on all sides.

On light / print backgrounds

  • Minimum size: never render the lockup narrower than 120px (digital) or 25mm (print) wide — the circuit joints are the first detail to blur out.
  • On dark surfaces (default): place directly on Void Black or Gunmetal. The cyan glow is calibrated for this — it's the brand's natural habitat.
  • On light surfaces: use only for print backgrounds like #F7F9FB or white. Never place on a mid-tone or busy photo without a dark scrim behind it.
  • Lockup: the "A"-mark and the AURIX wordmark travel together. Use the mark alone only for small spaces — favicons, badges, a watch-face-sized app icon.

Avoid

  • Recoloring the metal — it stays silver/chrome, only the glow is brand-cyan.
  • Removing or flattening the glow outline; it's what separates AURIX from a generic "A" mark.
  • Stretching, skewing, rotating, or adding a drop shadow that isn't the specified cyan glow.
  • Rebuilding the wordmark in a different typeface — always use the supplied logo file for "AURIX" itself.

Graphic Language

Recurring Elements

A small kit of motifs, pulled directly from the logo, that ties every printed and digital surface back to the mark.

Circuit Trace

The robotic-arm line from the mark, used as a section divider or a border detail on banners and slide templates.

Hex Grid Texture

A faint background watermark (6–10% opacity) for poster margins, slide backgrounds and the website's dark sections.

Edge Glow

Cyan outline + soft glow marks anything interactive or important — primary buttons, the countdown, the winner's card.

Bracket Frame

Corner ticks (used throughout this guide) read as "technical spec," not decoration — apply to any boxed content on posters or the site.

Poster & Digital Creatives

Void Black base, logo top-center, Orbitron wordmark with the chrome-gradient + cyan glow treatment from the hero above. One Ignition Orange CTA chip is the only warm color on the page — that's what makes it findable.

  • Keep body copy (dates, venue, rules) in Titillium Web, never Orbitron — it turns unreadable below 24px.
  • Reserve the hex-grid or circuit-line texture for the bottom third only, so it never competes with headline text.
  • Social tiles (1:1, 9:16) reuse this exact layout, just recropped — don't redesign per platform.

Website

Same Void/Gunmetal base as print. Primary buttons get the cyan glow; secondary actions stay as quiet outlined ghosts. Event cards use the bracket-frame panel style from this guide — hairline borders, no drop shadows, no rounded corners.

  • Nav and footer sit on Gunmetal, never pure Void, to separate them from page content.
  • Icons: simple line-weight glyphs in Chrome or Cyan — no filled illustration style, it clashes with the metallic mark.
  • Motion: reserve glow-pulse and reveal animation for one hero moment per page, not every card on hover.

Decor, Signage & Collateral

AURIX
INNOVATE · BUILD · BEYOND
  • Entrance arch / backdrop: Void Black vinyl, logo centered, cyan up-lighting if available — the glow in the mark is a lighting cue, not just a graphic effect.
  • Standees & direction boards: Gunmetal background, Chrome text, one cyan bracket-frame per board; keep to a single line of Orbitron for the title, rest in Titillium Web.
  • ID badges / lanyards: Gunmetal card, small logo lockup top, name in Titillium Web 700, track color-coded with a 4mm bar in Cyan (Innovate/Build) or Orange (Beyond/finalists).
  • Certificates: flip to the light/print palette — Paper background, Ink text, logo in full color, a single thin Circuit Blue rule under the recipient's name.
